---
title: Migrate a Power BI report
description: Turn a Power BI report into a Rayfin app that reads its semantic model live, while Copilot rebuilds its pages, visuals and filters one page at a time. Experimental.
---

> [!WARNING]
> Migrating Power BI reports is an experiment. Turn it on in **Settings → Experiments**. It may
> change or be removed in a future update.

Fabricator can turn a Power BI report into a new Rayfin app. The app reads the report's semantic
model live, so its numbers come from the same measures and the same data. GitHub Copilot rebuilds
the report one page at a time, with [Graphein](https://github.com/spatney/graphein) charts: every
page, visual, filter and slicer, in the same arrangement and colors.

You end up with a deployed app that follows the report, and a `MIGRATION.md` file in the project
that lists what each report visual became and what Copilot couldn't rebuild exactly.

## How a migration works

1. You pick a report, and Fabricator checks what it can read of it.
2. You name the new app and deploy it, like any new project.
3. Meanwhile, Fabricator reads the report: its definition, its data model and images of its pages.
4. The first chat turn starts by itself. Copilot sets up the app and migrates the first page.
5. You migrate the other pages, one chat turn per page.

## Before you start

You need:

- The Azure CLI, signed in with an account that can open the report. Fabricator finds and reads
  reports with the Azure CLI's sign-in, which setup already asks for. See
  [Manage your accounts](/docs/start/accounts).
- Build permission on the report's semantic model. The app queries the model live, so you need to
  be allowed to query it.
- A semantic model in a shared workspace. Rayfin apps can't connect to a model in My workspace.
- A Fabric workspace to deploy the app to, as for any app. See
  [Deploy to Microsoft Fabric](/docs/ship/deploy).

For the most faithful result, you also need:

- Edit access to the report: the Contributor, Member or Admin role in its workspace. With it,
  Fabricator can read the report's definition.
- The report's workspace on a Fabric or Premium capacity, so Fabricator can export images of its
  pages.

When you pick a report, Fabricator checks what it can read of it. Paginated reports can't be
migrated yet.

## Turn on the experiment

1. Open **Settings** from the account menu.
2. Open **Experiments**.
3. Turn on **Migrate Power BI reports**.

![The Experiments section of Settings, with a warning that experiments may change, and the Team workspaces and Migrate Power BI reports switches.](/screenshots/settings-experiments.webp)

Home now has **Migrate a Power BI report**. Turning the experiment off hides it and the Migration
card. It doesn't change the apps you migrated or delete their migration material.

## Pick a report

1. On Home, select **Migrate a Power BI report**.
2. Find the report in one of these ways:
   - Type at least two characters of its name in **Find a report** to search for it across your
     organization.
   - Select a workspace in the list, then the report. The workspaces your apps deploy to come
     first, then My workspace and the rest.
   - Copy the report's link from Power BI, paste it into **Find a report** and press **Enter**.
     Links to a report in a workspace, in My workspace or in a Power BI app all work.
3. Select the report. Fabricator reads it and shows its workspace, the semantic model it gets its
   data from, its pages and three checks.
4. When the report can be migrated, select **Continue**.

![The Migrate a Power BI report screen. Under Find a report, the hint names the Azure CLI account, and the workspace list starts with Contoso Apps, where the user's apps deploy. Sales analytics is open, with Sales performance picked. Below, the report's workspace, its semantic model Sales model and its five pages, the Definition, Data model and Page images checks all passing, and Continue.](/screenshots/migrate-report.webp)

The hint under **Find a report** names the Azure CLI account that Fabricator reads with, for
example "Reports you can open as avery.chen@contoso.com, through the Azure CLI." To use another
account, see [Use more than one Azure CLI account](/docs/start/accounts#use-more-than-one-azure-cli-account).

## What the checks mean

Each check shows a dot and a message. A warning means the migration can go ahead with less to
work from. An error means the report can't be migrated, and **Continue** stays off.

| Check | What Fabricator checks | If it can't |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Definition** | That you can edit the report, so it can read the report's definition: its pages, visuals, fields, filters, slicers and theme. | A warning. Copilot works from the page images and text, and finds the fields in the semantic model itself. |
| **Data model** | That you can query the report's semantic model. The app reads the model live, so this needs Build permission on it. | An error, such as "You can't query “Sales model”. Ask its owner for Build permission." |
| **Page images** | That the report's workspace is on a Fabric or Premium capacity, so the pages can be exported to PDF. Copilot looks at each page and checks its numbers against the page's text. | A warning. Copilot works from the definition only. |

A report also can't be migrated when Fabricator can read neither its definition nor images of its
pages: "Fabricator can neither read this report's definition nor export its pages." For the other
reasons, see [A report can't be migrated](#a-report-cant-be-migrated).

## Name and create the app

After **Continue**, the **New app from Power BI** screen opens.

1. Check the **Project name**. It starts as the report's name, without characters that project
   names can't have, such as parentheses.
2. Check **From Power BI**, which describes the report: its name, its workspace, how many pages it
   has and the semantic model it gets its data from.
3. Under **Copilot model**, choose the model that rebuilds the report. Fabricator remembers it for
   your next migration, and you can change the model in the chat later, between pages.
4. If you use team workspaces, choose **Where** the app goes: **Just me, on this computer** or a
   team workspace.
5. Select **Create project**.
6. In **Deploy your app**, choose a workspace and select **Deploy app**. When the report's
   workspace can host Rayfin apps, it's listed first, under **Recent**.

The app starts from the Universal App, the Rayfin CLI's default template, like any new project.
See [Create a new project](/docs/build/projects#create-a-new-project). A team app skips the
deploy step, because the team pipeline deploys your preview. See
[Work on a team app](/docs/team/work-on-an-app).

If you select **Continue without deploying →**, Fabricator still reads the report, but the first
page waits until you deploy the app.

## While Fabricator reads the report

While the app is created and deployed, Fabricator reads the report in the background. The
Migration card above the chat composer, "Migrating “Sales performance” from Power BI", shows each
stage:

| Stage | What Fabricator reads |
| --- | --- |
| **Report definition** | The pages, visuals, fields, filters, slicers, bookmarks and theme. |
| **Data model** | The semantic model's tables, columns, measures with their DAX, and relationships. |
| **Page export** | A PDF of the report's pages, exported by Power BI. It takes about 20 seconds a page, and the stage shows its progress as a percentage. |
| **Page images** | Each exported page, drawn as an image, and the text on it. |

Each stage shows **Waiting** until it starts, then **Working…** or a percentage while it runs. It
ends with **Done**, with **Skipped** when you skipped it or there was nothing to read, or with
**Not available** when Fabricator couldn't read it, with the reason below the stages. The
migration goes ahead with whatever Fabricator could read.

- To go on without page images, select **Skip page images** while the pages export. Copilot then
  works from the definition.
- If Fabricator can't read the semantic model's definition, it reads the model's tables, columns
  and measures with queries instead. The measures' DAX isn't included then, so Copilot works from
  their names and checks its results against the page text.

## The first page starts by itself

Once Fabricator has read the report and the app is deployed, the first chat turn starts by
itself. Its message says "Migrate “Sales performance” from Power BI". It carries the first page's
image, when Fabricator could export the pages, and a chip with the report's name and, for example,
"Setup and page 1 of 5: Overview".

In this turn, Copilot:

1. Turns on the capabilities the app needs for analytics, and adds Graphein, the charting library
   the app's visuals are built with.
2. Connects the report's semantic model live, through a Rayfin semantic model connector. See
   [Rayfin's semantic models docs](https://rayfin.ai/docs/connectors/semantic-models).
3. Adds a page for each report page, with the same names in the same order. Drillthrough and
   tooltip pages become detail views and tooltips instead of pages of their own.
4. Applies the report-level filters to every page, and carries the report's colors into the
   app's theme and charts.
5. Migrates the first page. For a report with only one page, it also builds the views the page's
   bookmarks show and wires its buttons.
6. Starts `MIGRATION.md`.

When the turn ends, Fabricator deploys the app, as it does after any chat turn, unless you turned
off **Deploy after each chat turn**. See [Redeploy changes](/docs/ship/deploy#redeploy-changes).

A migration's turns start only while the project is open on **Build** and nothing else is running.
Until then, the card says what it's waiting for, such as:

- "The first page starts once the app is deployed."
- "Waiting for the deploy to finish."
- "Waiting for Copilot to finish."

## Migrate the other pages

Once Fabricator has read the report, the card lists its pages, with an image of each, in the
order Copilot migrates them. It counts the pages done, such as "1 of 5 pages". Visible pages come
first, in the report's order, then drillthrough pages, tooltip pages and any other hidden pages.

![The Migration card above the chat composer: Migrating “Sales performance” from Power BI, 1 of 5 pages, a thumbnail of each of the five pages with Overview migrated, the note Next: “Regions”, and the Migrate next page and Migrate the rest buttons.](/screenshots/migration-card.webp)

- Select **Migrate next page** to migrate the next page in one chat turn. Its message says, for
  example, "Migrate page 2 of 5: Regions", with an image of that page.
- Select **Migrate the rest** to migrate the remaining pages one after another, one page per
  turn. Each page waits until the deploy after the previous page has finished. To stop once the
  current page is done, select **Stop after this page**.
- Sending a message of your own pauses **Migrate the rest**. Select it again to carry on.
- If a page doesn't migrate, it shows **Try again**.

Each page is a normal chat turn: you can follow its work log, review its changed files and change
the result in chat. See [Chat with Copilot](/docs/build/chat).

With the last page, Copilot also wires up the report's buttons, bookmarks and drillthroughs across
pages, and checks the app against `MIGRATION.md`. The card then says "Every page is migrated. MIGRATION.md lists what’s approximated."
Select **Close** (**×**) to close the card.

## What carries over

Copilot aims for a faithful rebuild: every page, visual, filter and slicer, in the same order,
arrangement and colors, on a layout that also fits smaller screens.

- **Numbers.** Copilot writes each visual's query with the same fields, aggregations and filters,
  runs it against the semantic model, and checks the result against the numbers on the exported
  page. The app shows live values from the model, not numbers copied from the report.
- **Filters and slicers.** Report, page and visual filters carry over. Slicers become filter
  controls that start from the slicer's saved selection. Changing one runs the page's queries
  again, so the model calculates every measure for the new selection, as in Power BI.
- **Interactions.** Where the report cross-filters, selecting part of a chart filters the page.
  Buttons and bookmarks become navigation or saved filter states, and a drillthrough becomes a
  link to its detail view.

Copilot rebuilds the visuals with [Graphein](https://github.com/spatney/graphein), a charting
library designed for coding agents: before Copilot builds on a chart, Graphein checks it for
mistakes and for labels that overlap or don't fit, and renders an image Copilot compares with the
report's page.

| In the report | In the app |
| --- | --- |
| Cards and KPIs | KPI cards, with the report's goals and trends |
| Multi-row cards | Groups of KPI cards |
| Gauges | Gauges |
| Bar, column, line, area, combo, ribbon, waterfall, funnel, pie, donut, scatter charts and treemaps | The same kind of chart, stacked or with a second axis where the report has one |
| Tables | Tables |
| Matrices | Matrices, with the report's row and column groups and totals |
| Slicers | Filter controls: dropdowns, lists, search boxes, ranges and date ranges |
| Text boxes, images, shapes and buttons | Text, images, layout and navigation |
| Maps | A filled or bubble map when the data has the regions or coordinates; otherwise a ranked bar chart by location |
| Custom visuals | The closest Graphein chart, such as a bullet chart for a bullet chart visual |
| R and Python visuals, Q&A, decomposition trees, key influencers, smart narratives, and Power Apps and Power Automate visuals | The closest chart that shows the same data, or a clearly labelled placeholder |

Compare each page with the report in the preview. To change something, describe it in chat.

### MIGRATION.md

Copilot keeps `MIGRATION.md` at the root of the project and updates it with every page. It lists:

- the source report and semantic model,
- for each page, what each report visual became and which file it's in,
- under **Approximations and gaps**, everything that isn't an exact match, and why.

`MIGRATION.md` is committed with the app like any other project file, so Copilot keeps data values
out of it.

## Where the report's material lives

Fabricator saves what Copilot works from in the project, in a folder named after the report under
`.fabricator/migration/`:

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md` | The report, its semantic model, and each page's visuals with their fields and filters. Copilot reads it first. |
| `report.json` | The report's definition: its pages, visuals with their positions and fields, filters, slicers, buttons, bookmarks and theme. |
| `model.md` | The semantic model's tables, columns, measures with their DAX, and relationships. |
| `theme.json` and `resources/` | The report's colors, and the images it uses, such as logos. |
| `pages/` | An image of each page and the text on it. |

The folder also keeps the exported PDF, the definition's original files and Graphein's guide,
which Copilot downloads for the version the app uses. Copilot keeps its own working files that
show data there too, such as the chart images it renders to check its work.

This material stays on this computer:

- The page images and text show real data from the report, so Fabricator keeps `.fabricator/` out
  of git. It lists the folder in the repository's `.git/info/exclude` file, so none of the app's
  own files change. The material isn't committed, so it doesn't go to GitHub with the app, team
  apps included.
- The app itself doesn't use the material. Once every page is migrated, you can delete the
  `.fabricator/migration` folder to remove the material from this computer. The Migration card
  goes with it.
- Copilot reads the material during the migration's chat turns, and each page's message carries
  an image of the page, so they reach the model you chose like the rest of the conversation. A
  model on your own API key that can't read images gets the messages without the images. See
  [Privacy and telemetry](/docs/reference/privacy#power-bi-report-migrations).

## Share a migrated app

A migrated app reads the semantic model as each person who uses it, with their own identity. The
model's row-level security applies, so each person sees only the data they're allowed to see.
Blueprint shows which identity each of the app's connections uses; see
[Which identity a connection uses](/docs/build/data-model#which-identity-a-connection-uses).

So everyone who uses the app needs Build permission on the semantic model. **Share** takes care of
it: for each person you share the app with, it grants Build on the semantic models the app
connects to through Rayfin connectors, when a model is in another workspace than the app. A model
in the app's own workspace is covered by the **Contributor** role that sharing grants on that
workspace. See [Share your app](/docs/ship/share).

## If Fabricator closes during a migration

- Reading the report picks up where it stopped the next time you open the project.
- A page whose turn was cut off shows **Try again**.
- If the first page hadn't started yet, it starts by itself once the app is deployed and
  Fabricator has read the report.

## Troubleshooting

### Fabricator asks you to sign in to the Azure CLI

On the **Migrate a Power BI report** screen, you see this message, or one like it:

> Sign in to the Azure CLI again (run az login), then try again.

Fabricator reads reports with the Azure CLI's sign-in, and that sign-in has expired or is
missing.

1. Sign in to the Azure CLI again: run `az login` in a terminal, or open **Accounts** and, under
   **Azure CLI**, select **Add account**.
2. Select **Try again** if the screen offers it, or pick the report again.

### The report isn't listed

The report you want isn't in its workspace's list or in the search results.

Fabricator lists the reports that the Azure CLI's account can open, and that account may not be
the one you use in Power BI.

1. Check the account named under **Find a report**. If it's the wrong one, switch accounts. See
   [Azure CLI is signed in to the wrong account](/docs/troubleshooting/setup-and-sign-in#azure-cli-is-signed-in-to-the-wrong-account).
2. Open the report in Power BI, copy its link from the browser's address bar, paste it into
   **Find a report** and press **Enter**.

### A report can't be migrated

**Continue** stays off, and Fabricator says why, in the **Data model** check or below the checks:

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "You can't query “Sales model”. Ask its owner for Build permission." | Ask the semantic model's owner for Build permission, then pick the report again. |
| "Fabricator can neither read this report's definition nor export its pages." | Get edit access to the report, or put its workspace on a Fabric or Premium capacity. Then pick the report again. |
| "Its semantic model is in My workspace, and Rayfin apps connect to models in shared workspaces. Publish the report to a workspace first, then migrate it from there." | Publish the report and its semantic model to a shared workspace, then migrate the report from there. |
| "Paginated reports can't be migrated yet." | Build the app in chat instead, and connect the data it needs. See [Connect Fabric data](/docs/build/data-model#connect-fabric-data). |
| "This report is in an app. Open it from its workspace and paste that link, or ask the app's owner for access to the workspace." | Paste the report's link from its workspace, or ask the app's owner for access to that workspace. |
| "This report isn't connected to a semantic model." | Pick a report that gets its data from a semantic model. |

### Fabricator can't read the report's definition

**Definition** says:

> You can view this report but not edit it, so its definition can't be read. Copilot will work from the page images and text.

On the Migration card, **Report definition** can also show **Not available**, with the reason
"You need edit access to this report to read its definition."

Reading a report's definition needs the Contributor, Member or Admin role in the report's
workspace. Without the definition, Copilot works from the page images and text, which is less
exact.

1. Ask an admin of the report's workspace for the Contributor role.
2. Pick the report again and check that **Definition** no longer shows a warning.

Fabricator reads a report once per migration. If you already started the migration, migrate the
report again to use its definition.

### The pages can't be exported

**Page images** says:

> This workspace isn't on a Fabric or Premium capacity, so pages can't be exported. Copilot will work from the definition only.

Or, on the Migration card, **Page export** shows **Not available**, with Power BI's reason below
the stages.

Power BI exports a report's pages only when:

- the report's workspace is on a Fabric or Premium capacity. Workspaces on a shared capacity, as
  with Power BI Pro, and Premium Per User workspaces can't export them.
- the tenant setting "Export reports as PowerPoint presentations or PDF documents" is on. It's on
  by default, and your Fabric administrator controls it.

Without page images, Copilot works from the definition, but it can't see what the pages look like
or check its numbers against them.

1. Move the report's workspace to a Fabric or Premium capacity, or publish the report to a
   workspace that's on one. If the tenant setting is off, ask your Fabric administrator to turn it
   on.
2. Migrate the report again. Fabricator exports the pages once per migration.

### A page needs another try

A page on the Migration card shows **Try again**.

The page's chat turn didn't finish, for example because of a Copilot error or because Fabricator
closed during it. **Migrate the rest** stops at a page that doesn't finish.

1. Read the message at the end of the turn in chat. For Copilot errors, see
   [Chat and Copilot problems](/docs/troubleshooting/chat).
2. Under the page on the card, select **Try again**.

### People you share the app with don't see its data

People you shared the app with can open it, but its visuals don't load their data.

The app reads the semantic model as each person who uses it, so each of them needs Build
permission on the model.

1. Share the app from Fabricator with **Share**. It grants Build on the models the app reads from
   other workspaces, and the Contributor role on the app's workspace, which covers the models
   there.
2. If people got access to the app another way, ask the semantic model's owner to give them Build
   permission.

Each person still sees only the rows that the model's row-level security lets them see.

If a problem isn't listed here or a fix doesn't work,
[report a problem](/docs/troubleshooting/report-a-problem).
